newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Dong to lay new North Sea gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Dong to lay new North Sea gas pipeline.

text.p: Denmark's state-owned Dansk Olie og Naturgas (DONG) said on Monday that it planned to lay a new natural gas pipeline from two Danish North Sea fields to its Nybro treatment plant, increasing total transmission capacity to 40 million cubic metres per day from a current 26 milion cubic metres.

A DONG statement said that the 300 km (190 mile) pipeline would run from the new Syd Arne field, operated by Amerada Hess, with a connection to DUC's Harald field. Future new fields could, also connect, it added.
Completion of the project was scheduled for 1999.
DONG said that it would buy the Syd Arne gas, about 700 million cubic metres a year.
The field, expected to start producing in mid-1999, is also expected to produce about 50,000 barrels per day of oil, equal to 20 percent of current production in the Danish North Sea.
The oil will be shipped by tanker from a loading buoy.
